newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds back off as rate hike fears continue.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds back off as rate hike fears continue.

text.p: Irish bonds backed off slightly on Wednesday afternoon after a good morning performance, as speculation over further U.S. interest rate hikes resurfaced to jangle market nerves, dealers said.

"Prices have fallen back since lunchtime in line with other markets pushed down by lower Treasuries," a dealer said. "It was sparked off by hints in the press by an unnamed Fed official that further rate rises are likely."
With little domestic or UK information expected this week players were focusing on Friday's non-farm payrolls data for pointers to the Federal Reserve's next move, dealers said.
"If it's a strong payroll number we'll see prices drop lower."
Compared to good buying interest earlier in the day, afternoon volumes were very thin, dealers said.

Whereas the Irish market outperformed other core European markets, including Germany, in early trade, the afternoon saw a narrowing of the spread on the five-year bonds to 151 basis points over Bunds, and on the 10-years to 94 basis points.

By 1600 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up five pence from Tuesday's close at 101.00 to yield 6.22 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up five pence from the close at 107.00 to yield 6.95 percent.
Looking ahead, the Irish market was awaiting domestic borrowing figures for the first quarter, and Central Bank statistics, both due on Thursday. -- Kevin Smith, Dublin newsroom + 353 1 661 3377
